item.title: 1Password discloses breach after GitHub account compromise
item.description:
1Password discloses breach after GitHub account compromise

1Password disclosed a data breach after an employee’s corporate GitHub account was hacked. The attacker used the compromised account to deploy malicious code to the company’s backend services to steal customer data.

🔍 Overview

The company began investigating the breach on November 19 after detecting indications that an employee’s GitHub account had been compromised. 1Password states that customer password vaults and the encryption keys protecting them were not compromised in the attack.

🧩 How it works

The attacker accessed private source code repositories and injected malicious code into backend services that downloaded customer account records. The malicious code also stole internal company source code and accessed the company’s continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) environment, potentially exposing internal infrastructure credentials.

⚙️ Key details

The following customer data was stolen in the breach:

  • Customer names and email addresses
  • Account and user IDs
  • Account creation and last sign-in timestamps
  • Public cryptographic keys
  • Secure Remote Password (SRP) protocol parameters
  • Invitation, provisioning, and account recovery tokens
  • Other internal account metadata

The stolen tokens were embedded in links that 1Password emailed to users to accept account provisioning invitations or recover their accounts. 1Password says these tokens cannot be used on their own to access customer accounts, as completing the invitation or recovery process requires either single sign-on (SSO) authentication or a six-digit verification code sent to the user’s registered email address.

🚀 Availability

1Password has disabled the compromised GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, restored clean versions of affected services, and rotated or revoked potentially exposed infrastructure credentials. The company has also hired independent cybersecurity experts to validate its remediation efforts. As a precaution against brute-force attacks, 1Password has strengthened these verification codes from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric characters. The company states that only a small number of users were affected and have been individually notified.

💡 Why it matters

While customer vaults were not compromised, the stolen data is valuable to threat actors as it provides a list of known 1Password users who could be targeted in phishing campaigns. Threat actors could send emails impersonating 1Password, using the breach as a lure to trick customers into disclosing their account passwords, Secret Keys, or recovery verification codes. 1Password is not requiring customers to change their account passwords or Secret Keys but warns them to watch for unexpected invitations, account recovery requests, and other potential phishing attempts.

#1Password #DataBreach #CyberSecurity #GitHub #Phishing

Source: 1Password customer data stolen after employee GitHub account breach

item.title: GitHub Builds AI-Powered Conference Badge for Hands-On Learning
item.description:
GitHub Builds AI-Powered Conference Badge for Hands-On Learning

🎮 Playful Hacking at GitHub Universe

For the last four years at GitHub Universe, we’ve had hackable conference badges. What started as a simple e-ink display for your name and job title morphed into a labor of love for Martin Woodward, VP of Developer Relations. This year, the badge evolved into a device with a color screen, rechargeable battery, accelerometer sensors, and touch-sensitive gaming controls.

🤖 AI Accelerates Code Creation

According to the Octoverse report, 40% of pull requests were started by agents by September. That’s a big jump from the 17% we saw in March, which was already a pretty high number. AI can turn our ideas into working code faster than ever before.

🏃 Learning Through Building

At the GitHub Universe closing keynote, Martin wanted to teach himself machine learning, so he built himself a pedometer onto his conference badge. He used Copilot to collect movement data from the badge’s accelerometer, trained a simple machine-learning model in his browser, and deployed it to the badge. Then he walked around to test whether it could tell the difference between walking, standing still, and fidgeting.

⚖️ Balancing Innovation and Open Source Values

We’re seeing maintainers get absolutely hammered with AI-powered contributions to their repositories, which adds a lot to the maintenance burden. As Martin explained in the keynote, “Open source is the freedom to inspect, to remix, and to share without asking for permission. But it’s not the freedom to impose your will on others.”

🎮 Gaming on the Badge

We answered the perennial question on our badge, “But can it run Doom?” Why yes, yes it does.

📣 Getting Your Own Badge

Plus, use code FREESHIPBLOG26 for free standard shipping through December 1, 2026. We made some extra badges just for you. Order yours today, then tell us what you’ll be building.

#AI #OpenSource #MachineLearning #GitHub

Source: Art of play in the age of AI

item.title: SafeLine Emerges as Top GitHub Trending WAF Repository
item.description:
SafeLine Emerges as Top GitHub Trending WAF Repository

SafeLine has newly appeared as a top-ranked GitHub trending repository for Go projects, establishing itself as a self-hosted Web Application Firewall (WAF) designed to protect web applications from attacks and exploits.

🔍 Overview

SafeLine is a self-hosted Web Application Firewall (WAF) to protect web apps from attacks and exploits. A web application firewall helps protect web apps by filtering and monitoring HTTP traffic between a web application and the Internet.

🧩 How it Works

Unlike a proxy server that protects a client machine’s identity, a WAF operates as a reverse-proxy, shielding the server by routing client requests through the firewall before reaching the server. A WAF protects web apps by filtering, monitoring, and blocking malicious HTTP/S traffic while preventing unauthorized data from leaving the application. This is achieved through policies that distinguish between malicious and safe traffic.

⚙️ Key Details

SafeLine’s core capabilities include:

Capability Description
Block Web Attacks Defends against SQL injection, XSS, code injection, os command injection, CRLF injection, XXE, SSRF, path traversal, and other web attacks
Rate Limiting Thwarts DoS attacks, bruteforce attempts, traffic surges, and abuse by throttling excessive traffic
Anti-Bot Challenge Blocks bots and crawlers while allowing human users through challenge mechanisms
Authentication Challenge Requires password entry for visitors when enabled, blocking unauthenticated access
Dynamic Protection Dynamically encrypts HTML and JavaScript code with each visit to the web server

Additional features include defenses for web attacks, proactive bot abuse defense, HTML & JS code encryption, IP-based rate limiting, and Web Access Control List.

🚀 Availability

SafeLine has achieved significant recognition on GitHub:

  • #1 GitHub Trending Repository
  • #1 Go Repository of the Day
  • #1 Go Repository of the Week
  • #9 Go Repository of the Month

💡 Why It Matters

The rise of SafeLine highlights growing community interest in self-hosted, open-source security solutions for web application protection, offering organizations an auditable alternative to commercial WAF offerings.

#WAF #cybersecurity #GoLang #GitHub #WebSecurity

Source: chaitin/SafeLine

item.title: Official code repository released for the book 'Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch)'
item.description:
Official code repository released for the book ‘Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch)’

An official code repository has been released for the book Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch). The repository contains the code required for developing, pretraining, and finetuning a GPT-like large language model (LLM).

🔍 Overview

The book is designed to teach readers how large language models work from the inside out by coding them from the ground up, step by step. The method described for training a small-but-functional model for educational purposes mirrors the approach used in creating large-scale foundational models such as those behind ChatGPT. The guide includes clear text, diagrams, and examples to explain each stage of the process.

⚙️ Key details

  • Includes code for loading the weights of larger pretrained models for finetuning.
  • The README.md file is a Markdown file; if downloaded from the Manning website, users are recommended to use a Markdown editor or previewer for proper viewing.
  • Ghostwriter is suggested as a free option for a Markdown editor.
  • Users can view the files directly on GitHub in a browser, which renders Markdown automatically.
  • Guidance on installing Python, Python packages, and setting up the code environment is available in the setup/README.md file within the setup directory.

🚀 Availability

The code repository is available on GitHub at https://github.com/rasbt/LLMs-from-scratch. Users can download a copy by clicking the Download ZIP button or by executing a terminal command to download the archive. Those who downloaded the code bundle from the Manning website are advised to visit the official GitHub repository for the latest updates.

#LLM #GitHub #Manning #CodeRepository

Source: rasbt/LLMs-from-scratch

item.title: GitHub Replica: Open Source Design Harness with AI
item.description:
GitHub Replica: Open Source Design Harness with AI

GitHub has launched Replica, an open-source design harness that leverages reinforcement learning to enable AI-generated prototypes within design systems. This tool allows developers and designers to create, refine, and collaborate on prototypes using GitHub Copilot.

🔍 Overview

  • Replica is an open-source design harness that considers the role of designers in the era of AI.
  • It focuses on reinforcement learning to improve over time based on user interactions and comments.
  • Replica can be adapted to fit various teams’ products and workflows.

🧩 How it works

  • Replica enables the creation of AI-generated prototypes within design systems.
  • Prototypes can be refined side-by-side with GitHub Copilot.
  • Prototypes can be published to a Replica Hub for collaboration, comments, and iteration.
  • The system learns from interactions and comments to improve over time.

⚙️ Key details

  • Replica started as an internal project but was shared with the community due to its usefulness.
  • It is open source, allowing for customization and adaptation.
  • The tool is designed to enable prototyping and collaboration in the age of AI.

🚀 Availability

  • Replica is available as an open-source project for developers and designers to use and adapt.

💡 Why it matters

  • Replica addresses the need for designers in the AI era by providing a tool for creating and refining prototypes.
  • It promotes collaboration and continuous improvement through reinforcement learning.
  • The open-source nature of Replica allows for customization and adaptation to various workflows.

#GitHub #Replica #OpenSource #Design #AI #Prototyping

item.title: LearnPrompt and associated agent skills gain 800+ GitHub stars
item.description:
LearnPrompt and associated agent skills gain 800+ GitHub stars

LearnPrompt, described as the account’s earliest public project, has been updated with a suite of agent skills and automated tools. The project recently reached a milestone of 800+ stars within one month of launch. The update includes the AI News Radar’s ‘伯乐’ skill, which automated the maintenance of the radar tool, and a new collection of 14 installable Agent Skills designed for heavy agent users.

🧩 Core Features

The ecosystem now centers on several key tools:

  • AI News Radar: Utilizes GitHub Actions, web interfaces, and automated summaries to monitor AI and tech information sources. It determines the value of new sources via a 7-day cooling-off period, checks for content duplication, and identifies stable integration methods. Its first application was upgrading ai-news-radar from v0.6 to v0.7.0, merging 4 PRs in a single dialogue.
  • Information Monitoring Methodology: Establishes a public method for monitoring information sources that involves fixed scraping criteria, daily snapshots, historical comparisons, and report generation, with results posted to a GitHub Pages site.
  • 淘金小镇: Tracks daily AI skill trends starting from ClawHub Top 100, expanding to monitor update logs (e.g., Claude Code) and model leaderboards (e.g., AA Index) with minimal environment dependencies.
  • Humanize PPT: Processes over 50 TED speeches to analyze main themes, audience perception, and narrative order before generating PPT content.

item.title: Managing AI-Generated Pull Request Descriptions with HTML Details and Summary Tags
item.description:
Managing AI-Generated Pull Request Descriptions with HTML Details and Summary Tags

Developers are increasingly utilizing coding agents like Claude Code and Codex to open pull requests (PRs) and manage project changes. While these agents generate accurate and comprehensive descriptions—detailing the problem, the solution, and verification steps—the volume of text can be overwhelming, leading to the use of specific Markdown techniques to organize information for human reviewers.

🧩 How it works

GitHub Markdown supports the HTML <details><summary> elements, which render as a collapsed heading that can be expanded to view larger blocks of text. This feature allows developers to bundle agent-written content behind a concise, human-curated summary:

  • The <summary> tag serves as the clickable line of text that acts as a summary.
  • The <details> element wraps the rest of the content to keep it hidden until expanded.
  • A carefully selected opening paragraph provides a high-level explanation to get readers up to speed.
  • The full agent-written description is placed within the tags to prevent the reader’s eyes from glazing over.
  • Screenshots are sometimes included to quickly illustrate new features.

⚙️ Key details

To maintain clarity, the order of the tags can be remembered using the five-syllable mnemonic “details-summary.” Developers use the summary line to identify the source and intensity of the AI work.

Attribute Usage in PR Summary
Model Name Identifies the specific agent used, such as Claude Opus 5.5.
Effort Level Indicates the intensity of the work, such as “Medium”.
Human Judgement Used to select the short opener or extract a summary from the agent’s text.

💡 Why it matters

Using the <details><summary> structure ensures that the PR remains a functional unit of work for bundling commits and documenting decisions without sacrificing readability. It provides a promise to the reader that the visible text represents human judgment on what is worth their time, while keeping the exhaustive agent-generated verification steps and data accessible for those who need it.

#GitHub #AIagents #ClaudeCode #Markdown #PullRequests

Source: Hide your slop PR descriptions behind

item.title: GitHub Octoverse 2026 Shows Tripling of Commits and Pull Requests Driven by Agentic Engineering
item.description:
GitHub Octoverse 2026 Shows Tripling of Commits and Pull Requests Driven by Agentic Engineering

GitHub’s 2026 Octoverse report, announced by EVP Jay Parikh, reveals a sharp rise in development activity that the report links to the rise of “agentic engineering.”

📈 Overview

  • The report describes a “pretty stark representation of the impact of agentic engineering on GitHub.”
  • Growth is most pronounced in the second half of the year.

📊 Key Metrics

Metric Monthly Value (2026)
Merged pull requests 220 million
Commits 7.38 billion
New repositories 30.3 million

🤖 Agentic Engineering Impact

  • Agentic engineering is cited as the primary driver behind the observed surge in activity.

🛠️ AI‑Powered Methodology

  • Location normalization: LLM classification extracts ISO 3166‑1 alpha‑2 country codes from user profiles to adjust for VPN‑related bias.
  • Industry classification: A fine‑tuned multilingual embedding model maps public repositories (2022‑2026) to NAICS sectors using name, description, topics, and README.
  • Interoperability detection: Repositories are counted when their metadata mentions terms such as “interoperability,” “reverse engineering,” “clean room implementation,” “drop‑in replacement,” or “protocol re‑implementation.”

🌐 Industry & Interoperability Insights

  • The report breaks out activity by industry, based on the NAICS‑sector classification.
  • Separate counts are provided for repositories involving interoperability or reverse engineering.

#GitHub #Octoverse #AgenticEngineering #LLM

Source: GitHub Octoverse 2026

item.title: OpenHuman Open Source Agent Harness Launched with Local-First Memory
item.description:
OpenHuman Open Source Agent Harness Launched with Local-First Memory

OpenHuman has launched as an open source agent harness featuring agent orchestration, workflows, and local-first memory. Within one week of its launch, the project became the number one trending repository on GitHub for nine consecutive days.

🔍 Overview

OpenHuman is described as a personal AI super intelligence that functions as a deep researcher, an orchestrator, and a brain that remembers everything. It is not AGI.

🧩 How it works

OpenHuman provides three primary capabilities:

Feature Description
Brain Builds a persistent, local memory of your world
Orchestrator Runs fleets of agents on durable graphs
Deep Researcher Sweeps data and the web before a user finishes asking

⚙️ Key details

  • Memory Tree + Obsidian Wiki: Data is compressed into scored Markdown trees in SQLite on the user’s machine and mirrored as an Obsidian vault for opening and editing.
  • Integrations: The system includes 100+ OAuth integrations, 5,000+ MCP servers, and 90,000+ Skills for one-click access to tools such as GitHub, Slack, Notion, and Gmail.
  • Auto-fetch: A feature that feeds the brain every 20 minutes to provide updated context.

🚀 Availability

Installers are available via the GitHub Releases page or at tinyhumans.ai/openhuman.

#OpenHuman #OpenSource #AIAgents #GitHub

Source: tinyhumansai/openhuman

item.title: Tracking Pull Request Performance of Top SWE Coding Agents
item.description:
Tracking Pull Request Performance of Top SWE Coding Agents

A new repository tracks the opened and merged pull requests (PRs) from top software engineering (SWE) coding agents developed by OpenAI, GitHub, and other entities.

🔍 Overview

The repository categorizes pull requests into three types:

  • All PRs: Every pull request created by an agent, including DRAFT PRs.
  • Ready PRs: Non-draft pull requests that are ready for review and merging.
  • Merged PRs: Pull requests that were successfully merged into the codebase.

⚙️ Key details

Different agents utilize different workflows for PR creation:

  • Codex: Iterates privately and creates ready PRs directly, resulting in high merge rates and few drafts.
  • Copilot and Codegen: Create draft PRs first to encourage public iteration before marking them as ready for review.

To ensure a fair comparison across these different workflows, statistics focus on Ready PRs only.

📊 Agent Statistics

Agent Ready PRs Merged PRs Merge Rate
Copilot 1,606,114 1,542,535 96.04%
Codex 6,896,711 6,179,306 89.6%
Cursor 820,725 834,966 101.74%
Devin 244,909 150,954 61.64%
Codegen 5,628 3,462 61.51%
Jules 235,475 202,177 85.86%

#SWEagents #codingagents #GitHub #OpenAI
